topic: Entropic zero-set collapse and certified recovery of finite OT moment identified sets. Let two fixed finite alphabets have observed marginals p,q bounded below by eta, let pi range over Pi(p,q), let theta range over a computably covered compact set, and define D0(theta)=min_pi ||sum_ij pi_ij phi_ij(theta)|| for a bounded moment table with a known modulus and a nonempty sharp set Theta0 satisfying a displayed separation exponent kappa. Prove that adding epsilon KL(pi||p tensor q) yields D_epsilon=min_pi{||m_theta(pi)||+epsilon KL} and, for every epsilon>0, exact zero membership iff the product coupling satisfies the moment. Derive the pointwise first-order penalty as minimum KL over D0-minimizing couplings. Construct certified Sinkhorn primal-dual and rational-repair brackets L_a<=D0<=U_a with uniform gap at most a and finite polynomial work in fixed dimensions, then combine them with multinomial confidence events to give finite-sample simultaneous outer coverage of Theta0 and separation-based Hausdorff control on that same event. Credit Franguridi--Liu arXiv:2512.18084v3 for the regularized OT estimator and bootstrap, and generic entropy and criterion-set theory; exclude unconditional two-sided root-rate recovery and the refuted directional-face frontier. Their UAS attrition/refreshment workflow is the consumer, but its published contour is not characterized without a code audit. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The fresh presolve rederived D_epsilon=min_pi{||m_theta(pi)||+epsilon KL}, exact product-coupling zero-set collapse, and the fixed-instance J=min KL expansion. It solved the binary benefit-share case where [1/2,1] collapses to {3/4}, plus a vector tied-face case. It derived certified original-value brackets, exact marginal repair, an O(a^(-5)) exact-arithmetic per-query stopping bound, marginal stability, and finite-cell simultaneous coverage and Hausdorff control. A reproducible check covered 21 binary cases and 4,500 Sinkhorn iterates over 15 positive 3-by-3 problems against LP values. Destructive checks reproduced the current v3 entropy-normalization error, excluded the false face-bias and unconditional-rate claims, handled zero empirical cells by support reduction, and found no exact qid or theorem collision at the accepted tier. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove the finite-precision lemma giving polynomial total bit work for outward Sinkhorn dual evaluation and exact rational marginal repair, including accumulated-update, positivity, denominator-length, and exp/log precision budgets. EARLY KILL TEST: On the rational binary witness and a tied positive 3-by-3 table, construct outward dual enclosures and exact repairs as a decreases; stop or change the computation theorem if valid original-value brackets cannot be preserved with polynomial precision. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/pid_entropic_zero_set_collapse.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct an end-to-end finite-precision Sinkhorn certificate for finite OT moment values that outputs outward primal-dual bounds and an exactly marginal-feasible rational repair with polynomial total bit work.

source_refs.claim: Algorithm 2 returns an approximate Sinkhorn value after an unspecified convergence criterion and provides neither outward value enclosures nor a finite-precision stopping theorem.
source_refs.author: Grigory Franguridi and Laura Liu

source_refs.claim: Gives arithmetic-operation complexity and an exact-real rounding lemma controlled by marginal residuals, but does not propagate directed floating-point error into certified original-value brackets.
source_refs.author: Jason Altschuler, Jonathan Weed, and Philippe Rigollet

source_refs.claim: Analyzes approximate matrix scaling with inexact marginal computations and finite fixed-point parameters, but targets scaling residual rather than an outward certificate after rational repair.
source_refs.author: Joran van Apeldoorn, Sander Gribling, Yinan Li, Harold Nieuwboer, Michael Walter, and Ronald de Wolf

source_refs.claim: Provides rounding-error analysis for shifted log-sum-exp and softmax, isolating a stabilized-Sinkhorn primitive without covering accumulated updates or marginal repair.
source_refs.author: Pierre Blanchard, Desmond J. Higham, and Nicholas J. Higham

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing OT complexity results principally count exact-real arithmetic operations, while numerical analyses separately control log-sum-exp evaluations or approximate scaling residuals. A partial-identification certificate additionally requires outward dual evaluation, nonnegative rational primal repair with exact marginals, and a joint budget for accumulated potential-update error, exponentials, logarithms, positivity, and denominator growth. The located literature does not compose these components into certified lower and upper bounds for the original nonlinear moment value.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An algorithmic theorem that takes rational p, q, a bounded rational moment table, and tolerance a, returns rational L_a <= D_0(theta) <= U_a with U_a-L_a <= a and exact repaired marginals, and proves polynomial bounds on iterations, precision bits, denominator length, and total bit operations in fixed alphabet dimensions.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its progression from entropic smoothing through marginal rounding to an original-OT guarantee, while making the final guarantee independently checkable at bit level.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Exact OT is costly -> Sinkhorn rapidly produces a nearly feasible regularized plan -> rounding transfers approximate feasibility to the original problem -> outward arithmetic and exact repair should turn the approximation into a certificate.

method_exemplars.technique: Use marginal-residual-controlled truncation and rank-one deficit repair, then translate plan displacement into objective-value error.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired upper certificate requires the same move from an infeasible Sinkhorn iterate to a feasible coupling, augmented by exact rational and outward-error accounting.

method_exemplars.technique: Budget fixed-point errors in approximate marginal computations throughout Sinkhorn iterations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly addresses accumulated finite-precision perturbations of matrix scaling, the missing layer in exact-real OT complexity results.

method_exemplars.technique: Use shifted log-sum-exp formulas and forward-error bounds to construct directed enclosures for dual updates and value evaluations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Repeated log-sum-exp calls are the numerical primitive whose local enclosures must be composed into a global Sinkhorn certificate.

open_problems.open_problem: For finite positive marginals and a vector moment table, determine the exact zero set and first-order vanishing-entropy expansion of D_epsilon(theta)=min_pi{||m_theta(pi)||+epsilon KL(pi||p tensor q)}, including tied minimizing faces.

source_refs.claim: Defines regularization relative to the product marginal law and acknowledges regularization bias, but does not characterize the changed zero set; its displayed implementation also uses an unnormalized negative-entropy expression.
source_refs.author: Grigory Franguridi and Laura Liu

source_refs.claim: Provides explicit nonasymptotic entropy-penalty convergence for linear programs, but not the zero set or first-order coefficient of a norm-of-moment objective.
source_refs.author: Jonathan Weed

source_refs.claim: Establishes convergence of exponential-penalty trajectories to a distinguished linear-program optimum, leaving nonlinear moment-distance criteria outside its scope.
source_refs.author: Roberto Cominetti and Jaime San Martin

open_problems.why_unsolved: Entropic-OT theory mainly regularizes a linear transport cost, whereas this criterion minimizes a norm of a vector moment and may have a positive-dimensional minimizing face. Because product-relative KL is nonnegative and vanishes only at the product coupling, adding it may collapse a large sharp set for every positive epsilon. The first proof step that differs from linear-cost analyses is identifying and perturbing the entire argmin face of pi mapsto ||m_theta(pi)|| rather than following one LP cost vector; the KL-versus-negative-entropy normalization mismatch in the anchor paper also requires a normalization-explicit result.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem proving {theta:D_epsilon(theta)=0}={theta:m_theta(p tensor q)=0} for every epsilon>0 and lim_{epsilon downarrow 0}(D_epsilon(theta)-D_0(theta))/epsilon=min{KL(pi||p tensor q):pi in argmin D_0(theta)}, with an explicit regime statement for tied faces.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its marginal-information-to-OT-to-regularization arc while making the estimand change induced by regularization the central problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Only marginals are observed -> feasible couplings generate a sharp moment identified set -> entropy smooths computation but changes the population criterion -> characterize the exact zero-set collapse and leading penalty.

method_exemplars.technique: Compare penalized and unpenalized optima on a compact polytope and localize the penalized solution near the optimal face using explicit entropy ranges.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired first-order coefficient is likewise determined by entropy restricted to an unregularized optimal face, although that face here comes from a vector-moment norm.

method_exemplars.technique: Use exponential-penalty trajectories and optimal-face selection to isolate the entropy-selected limit.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the foundational selected-face analysis for entropic penalization and supplies the closest perturbation template.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply functional delta-method and empirical-process arguments for regularized OT values together with bootstrap consistency.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After population bias is characterized, this is the closest limit-theory template for an empirical regularized transport functional.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether exact finite-sample confidence events for finite multinomial marginals can be propagated through certified OT moment brackets to simultaneous outer coverage and separation-calibrated Hausdorff control of the sharp identified set.

source_refs.claim: Establishes asymptotic Hausdorff consistency under a high-level uniform criterion bound and uses a directionally differentiable bootstrap, but does not provide a finite-sample coverage event incorporating optimization error.
source_refs.author: Grigory Franguridi and Laura Liu

source_refs.claim: Develops criterion-level-set estimators, confidence regions, consistency, and rates for identified sets, primarily through asymptotic sample-criterion analysis.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Han Hong, and Elie Tamer

source_refs.claim: Constructs finite-sample multinomial confidence regions with uniform simplex coverage, but does not map them through an OT-defined criterion set.
source_refs.author: Matthew L. Malloy, Ardhendu Tripathy, and Robert D. Nowak

source_refs.claim: Provides likelihood-level-set multinomial regions with controlled nonasymptotic coverage in arbitrary finite dimension, including small samples.
source_refs.author: Djalil Chafai and Didier Concordet
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

open_problems.why_unsolved: Criterion-set theory gives a deterministic route from uniform criterion error and separation to set convergence, while multinomial theory gives exact confidence regions for p and q. Their composition with a computable OT value enclosure remains missing: the stability argument must hold uniformly over theta and all marginal pairs in the confidence event, and numerical tolerance must enter the inclusion on the same side as sampling error. Asymptotic bootstrap validity or Monte Carlo performance alone does not certify finite-sample simultaneous containment of the full sharp set.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite-sample theorem defining a computable outer set from multinomial confidence regions and brackets [L_a(theta),U_a(theta)], proving P(Theta_0 subseteq widehat Theta_out)>=1-alpha and, on the same event under D_0(theta)>=c d(theta,Theta_0)^kappa, an explicit Hausdorff bound proportional to ((sampling radius+a)/c)^(1/kappa).

writing_exemplar.why: Adopt its criterion-minimizer formulation and separation between estimating and covering an identified set, replacing asymptotic criterion control by one finite-sample event.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Economic restrictions define a zero or minimizer set -> sample criteria perturb that set -> level-set inversion gives outer confidence regions -> exact marginal events plus certified computation should yield simultaneous coverage and Hausdorff control.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert multinomial covering collections to obtain simplex regions with finite-sample uniform coverage.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The random inputs to the finite OT criterion are finite-alphabet marginal probability vectors.

method_exemplars.technique: Convert uniform criterion error plus a polynomial minorant or separation condition into outer inclusion and Hausdorff control for level sets.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested output is a confidence region for the zero set of a criterion with an explicit separation exponent.

method_exemplars.technique: Repair marginal infeasibility with controlled plan displacement and translate it into objective-value error.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the deterministic bridge needed to place numerical error inside the same event as multinomial sampling error.

open_problems.open_problem: Develop a data-driven joint rule for the entropy level, identified-set threshold, directional argmax threshold, and numerical tolerance that preserves honest coverage while adapting to unknown regularization bias and separation exponent.

source_refs.claim: Uses fixed regularization and high-level thresholds and proposes Lepskii-type bias-variance and bootstrap calibration ideas while leaving their full treatment for future work.
source_refs.author: Grigory Franguridi and Laura Liu

source_refs.claim: Provides limit distributions, efficiency, and bootstrap consistency for fixed regularized OT functionals, not adaptive recovery of an unregularized identified set over regularization levels.
source_refs.author: Ziv Goldfeld, Kengo Kato, Gabriel Rioux, and Ritwik Sadhu

source_refs.claim: Quantifies how empirical entropic-OT error depends on sample size, regularization, and marginal complexity, but does not combine adaptive regularization choice with identified-set coverage.
source_refs.author: Michel Groppe and Shayan Hundrieser

open_problems.why_unsolved: Selecting epsilon is nonstandard because changing epsilon changes the population zero set rather than merely estimator variance. The outer-set threshold must simultaneously dominate sampling, regularization, discretization, and finite-precision errors, while conversion to Hausdorff loss depends on an unknown separation exponent. Fixed-epsilon bootstrap theory and entropic-OT sample-complexity bounds do not establish post-selection coverage for this coupled four-way choice.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A Lepskii-style multiscale selection theorem with a fully specified joint rule for entropy, numerical, set-inversion, and directional thresholds, a uniform oracle inequality for the unregularized criterion, and honest outer-set coverage plus separation-adaptive Hausdorff control over a named class of finite moment models.

writing_exemplar.why: Use its practical tuning discussion and explicit future-work transition as the problem-formulation template.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Entropy trades bias for regular empirical behavior -> set and argmax inversion introduce further thresholds -> fixed tuning is only sensitivity-checked empirically -> a multiscale rule should adapt all tolerances while preserving coverage.

method_exemplars.technique: Use empirical-process linearization and bootstrap consistency for regularized OT to calibrate stochastic comparisons across candidate regularization levels.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The adaptive rule must compare empirical regularized transport criteria against scale-dependent stochastic fluctuations.

method_exemplars.technique: Use explicit regularization- and sample-size-dependent empirical OT bounds to construct scale-dependent penalties.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Those bounds expose the same bias-variance coordinates that a Lepskii rule must balance.

method_exemplars.technique: Use explicit entropy-penalty approximation bounds to construct deterministic regularization-bias envelopes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Honest adaptive selection needs deterministic bias control at each candidate entropy scale, not only pointwise convergence.

open_problems.open_problem: Extend certified zero-set recovery from two finite marginals to K finite marginals for causal quantities depending jointly on multiple potential outcomes while retaining a computable separation-based identified-set guarantee.

source_refs.claim: Lists extensions beyond two marginals, including multiple panel waves and repeated cross-sections, as future theoretical work.
source_refs.author: Grigory Franguridi and Laura Liu

source_refs.claim: Obtains causal partial-identified sets via multi-marginal OT and minimax plug-in rates for quadratic objectives, but not entropy-induced zero-set characterizations or certified recovery for general vector moments.
source_refs.author: Zijun Gao, Shu Ge, and Jian Qian

source_refs.claim: Provides arithmetic-operation complexity for multimarginal Sinkhorn approximation of linear MOT costs, including tensor-size dependence, but not certified vector-moment zero sets.
source_refs.author: Tianyi Lin, Nhat Ho, Marco Cuturi, and Michael I. Jordan

source_refs.claim: Shows that graph-structured entropy-regularized multimarginal OT can be computed through graphical-model inference, suggesting a route around dense tensor enumeration.
source_refs.author: Isabel Haasler, Rahul Singh, Qinsheng Zhang, Johan Karlsson, and Yongxin Chen

open_problems.why_unsolved: The causal multi-marginal literature covers exact partial identification for selected scalar quadratic objectives, while the optimization literature provides approximate arithmetic complexity for linear tensor costs. Neither treats a vector-moment norm as the population criterion, its collapse under KL relative to the product of K marginals, or outward value certificates that propagate into parameter-set guarantees. The first proof step that changes from the two-marginal construction is exact marginal repair: a rank-one two-way deficit correction does not automatically control every K-way marginal, while naive tensor output incurs exponential dependence on K.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A K-marginal theorem characterizing the entropy-regularized zero set and first-order KL penalty for vector moments, together with certified value brackets and a separation-based outer-coverage and Hausdorff result whose complexity is explicit in K and exploits a named graphical factorization when available.

writing_exemplar.why: Its multiple-potential-outcome framing is the closest destination-area motivation and avoids implying that the two-marginal donor paper posed this causal extension.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Each unit has several potential outcomes -> only their separate marginals are observed -> joint causal quantities form multi-marginal OT identified sets -> general vector moments require certified zero-set recovery rather than only quadratic plug-in bounds.

method_exemplars.technique: Transfer the potential-outcome-to-MOT reduction and empirical plug-in stability and minimax analysis for multiple observed marginals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It studies the same causal data-fusion geometry for K potential-outcome marginals, although for narrower objectives.

method_exemplars.technique: Use multimarginal Sinkhorn scaling, tensor marginal-residual accounting, and rounding-based approximation complexity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired certificate requires the same K-way scaling machinery before adding outward arithmetic and vector-moment bounds.

method_exemplars.technique: Exploit factorized costs and message-passing representations of entropic MOT to avoid materializing the full coupling tensor.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A useful K-marginal theorem needs structural conditions under which certified computation avoids full tensor storage.

literature_map:
Franguridi--Liu (2026, arXiv:2512.18084v3) is the direct anchor: marginal-only GMM, support-function OT identification, entropic estimation, and a directionally differentiable bootstrap.
Its population target is a regularized zero set while its text acknowledges bias; Algorithm 2 also exposes a KL-versus-negative-entropy normalization issue and lacks certified stopping.
Fan--Park--Pass--Shi (2025, arXiv:2503.16098) develops conditional-OT characterizations for incomplete-data moment models, clarifying the adjacent identification frontier.
Weed (2018, arXiv:1806.01879) and Cominetti--San Martin (1994, DOI 10.1007/BF01582220) analyze entropy penalties and selected optimal faces for linear programs, but not norm-valued vector-moment criteria.
Delalande (2022, arXiv:2110.12678) gives tight small-entropy cost expansions in semi-discrete quadratic OT, again under a classical transport-cost structure.
Altschuler--Weed--Rigollet (2017, arXiv:1705.09634) supplies Sinkhorn complexity and marginal rounding; Lin--Ho--Jordan (2022, arXiv:1906.01437) sharpens arithmetic complexity, but neither provides an end-to-end bit certificate.
Van Apeldoorn et al. (2021, arXiv:2011.12823) permit inexact marginal computations in matrix scaling, while Blanchard--Higham--Higham (2021, arXiv:1909.03469) analyze floating-point log-sum-exp; their composition into outward OT brackets appears unoccupied.
Mena--Niles-Weed (2019, arXiv:1905.11882), Klatt--Tameling--Munk (2020, DOI 10.1137/19M1278788), and Goldfeld--Kato--Rioux--Sadhu (2024, arXiv:2205.04283) establish CLTs, efficiency, and bootstrap theory for regularized OT, chiefly at fixed regularization.
Groppe--Hundrieser (2024, JMLR 25(344)) exposes explicit dependence of empirical entropic-OT error on regularization and sample size, useful for but not completing adaptive unregularized-set recovery.
Chernozhukov--Hong--Tamer (2007, DOI 10.1111/j.1468-0262.2007.00794.x), Romano--Shaikh (2010, DOI 10.3982/ECTA6706), and Bugni (2010, DOI 10.3982/ECTA8056) supply criterion-set and coverage frameworks, predominantly asymptotic.
Chafai--Concordet (2009, arXiv:0805.1971) and Malloy--Tripathy--Nowak (2021, arXiv:2002.01044) provide nonasymptotic multinomial regions; no located paper propagates them through certified OT computation to a Hausdorff guarantee.
Gao--Ge--Qian (2025, arXiv:2406.07868) already occupies multi-marginal causal partial identification for quadratic objectives, so a new direction must target general vector moments and certification rather than repeat MOT identification.
Lin--Ho--Cuturi--Jordan (2022, arXiv:1910.00152) and Haasler et al. (2021, arXiv:2006.14113) provide multimarginal Sinkhorn and graph-structured message-passing machinery for a non-verbatim extension.
Hirano--Imbens--Ridder--Rubin (2001, DOI 10.1111/1468-0262.00260) and recent raking or refreshment-sample work frame the UAS consumer, but its exact published data-processing contour still requires a code and data audit.
